arxiv-2202-04056.title: Spectroscopic orbits of subsystems in multiple stars. VIII.
arxiv-2202-04056.creator: Andrei Tokovinin
arxiv-2202-04056.description: Abstract Periods, eccentricities, and masses in hierarchical stellar systems inform us on the formation and early evolution of these fascinating objects. To complement the multiplicity statistics of nearby solar-type stars, 19 new spectroscopic orbits of inner subsystems in 15 hierarchies (10 triples and 5 quadruples) are determined based on high-resolution echelle spectra collected during several years.

arxiv-2206-09002.title: Cluster Generation via Deep Energy-Based Model
arxiv-2206-09002.creator: A. Yu. Artsukevichartsukevich@gmail.com, S. V. LepeshkinS.Lepeshkin@skoltech.ru
arxiv-2206-09002.description: Abstract We present a new approach for the generation of stable structures of nanoclusters using deep learning methods. Our method consists in constructing an artificial potential energy surface, with local minima corresponding to the most stable structures and which is much smoother than "real" potential in the intermediate regions of the configuration space.

arxiv-2208-10781.title: Object Detection in Aerial Images with Uncertainty-Aware Graph Network
arxiv-2208-10781.creator: Jongha Kim, Jinheon Baek, Sung Ju Hwang
arxiv-2208-10781.description: Abstract In this work, we propose a novel uncertainty-aware object detection framework with a structured-graph, where nodes and edges are denoted by objects and their spatial-semantic similarities, respectively. Specifically, we aim to consider relationships among objects for effectively contextualizing them.

arxiv-2210-05740.title: Stochastic Constrained DRO with a Complexity Independent of Sample Size
arxiv-2210-05740.creator: Qi Qi qi-qi@uiowa.edu
arxiv-2210-05740.description: Abstract Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO), as a popular method to train robust models against distribution shift between training and test sets, has received tremendous attention in recent years. In this paper, we propose and analyze stochastic algorithms that apply to both non-convex and convex losses for solving Kullback–Leibler divergence constrained DRO problem.

arxiv-2309-17155.title: Immersed figure-8 annuli and anyons
arxiv-2309-17155.creator: Bowen Shi
arxiv-2309-17155.description: Abstract Immersion (i.e., local embedding) is relevant to the physics of topologically ordered phases through the entanglement bootstrap. An annulus can be immersed in a disk or a sphere as a “figure-8”, which cannot be smoothly deformed to an embedded annulus.

arxiv-2405-01418.title: GTX: A Write-Optimized Latch-free Graph Data System with Transactional Support - Extended Version
arxiv-2405-01418.creator: Libin Zhou, Lu Xing, Yeasir Rayhan, Walid. G. Aref
arxiv-2405-01418.description: Abstract . This paper introduces GTX, a standalone main-memory write-optimized graph data system that specializes in structural and graph property updates while enabling concurrent reads and graph analytics through ACID transactions. Recent graph systems target concurrent read and write support while guaranteeing transaction semantics.

arxiv-2408-03493.title: Effect of neutrino electromagnetic properties on the quasielastic neutral-current neutrino-nucleus scattering
arxiv-2408-03493.creator: K. S. Kim, P. T. P. Hutauruk, Seung-il Nam, Chang Ho Hyun
arxiv-2408-03493.description: Abstract In the quasielastic region, we investigate the effect of neutrino electromagnetic properties constrained from the recent experiments on the electroweak neutral current reaction process of the neutrino- 12 C scattering. For a relativistic description of the nuclear dynamics, we employ the relativistic mean-field model, which has been proven to describe the data nicely in the quasielastic region.

arxiv-2504-18917.title: Meta-Learning in Self-Play Regret Minimization
arxiv-2504-18917.creator: David Sychrovský, Martin Schmid, Michal Šustr, Michael Bowling
arxiv-2504-18917.description: Abstract Regret minimization is a general approach to online optimization which plays a crucial role in many algorithms for approximating Nash equilibria in two-player zero-sum games. The literature mainly focuses on solving individual games in isolation. However, in practice, players often encounter a distribution of similar but distinct games.

arxiv-2510-03235.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Valentino Smaldore. In this note, we list many equivalent constructions of the tangent polar graph N ​ O + ​ ( 6 , 2 ) NO^{+}(6,2) . A strongly regular graph with parameters (v,k,\lambda,\mu) is a graph with v vertices where each vertex is incident with k edges, any two adjacent vertices have \lambda common neighbours, and any two non-adjacent vertices have \mu common neighbours. We denote it by srg(v,k,\lambda,\mu) .

pmc-10490996.title: 2-Methyl-4-chlorophenoxyacetic acid (MCPA) sorption and desorption as a function of biochar properties and pyrolysis temperature
pmc-10490996.creator: Abdullah Niaz, Kurt A Spokas, Bea Gámiz, David Mulla, Khaliq R Arshad, Sarfraz Hussain, Vusumzi Pakade
pmc-10490996.description: 2-Methyl-4-chlorophenoxyacetic acid (MCPA) is a highly mobile herbicide that is frequently detected in global potable water sources. One potential mitigation strategy is the sorption on biochar to limit harm to unidentified targets. However, irreversible sorption could restrict bioefficacy thereby compromising its usefulness as a vital crop herbicide.

pmc-11435325.title: Effects of Melatonin and 3,5,3′-Triiodothyronine on the Development of Rat Granulosa Cells
pmc-11435325.creator: Mingqi Wu, Yilin Yao, Rui Chen, Baoqiang Fu, Ying Sun, Yakun Yu, Yan Liu, Haoyuan Feng, Shuaitian Guo, Yanzhou Yang, Cheng Zhang, Josep Julve
pmc-11435325.description: Melatonin, as an endocrine neurotransmitter, can promote the development of the ovary. Meanwhile, it also has protective effect on the ovary as an antioxidant. Thyroid hormone (TH) is essential for normal human reproductive function. Many studies have shown that 3,5,3′-triiodothyronine (T3) regulates the development of ovarian granulosa cells.

pmc-12110474.title: Assessment of Dyslipidaemia and Cardiovascular Disease Risk Factors among Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients Attending Kabutare District Hospital, Huye, Rwanda
pmc-12110474.creator: Herbert Tendayi Mapira, Joseph Musangwa, Anselme Mugenga, Jessca Umurerwa, Dominique Ufitikirezi, Cuthbert Musarurwa
pmc-12110474.description: BackgroundDyslipidaemia is a major contributing factor to the development of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetic mellitus (T2DM) patients. People with T2DM are at a significantly high risk of developing dyslipidaemia which in turn is a risk factor for CVD. The objective of this study was to assess the risk factors for CVD in T2DM patients.

pmc-12767386.title: Development and Evaluation of an Innovative Inflammatory Prognostic Score for Predicting Long‐Term Mortality in Patients With Pulmonary Embolism
pmc-12767386.creator: Ning Zhu, Lei Zhang, Jiabao Wu, Fei Ye, Nanding Yu, Chao Cao, Limin Chen, Diogo Peruchetti
pmc-12767386.description: BackgroundSystemic inflammation is closely associated with adverse outcomes in pulmonary embolism (PE). This study aimed to develop and evaluate a novel inflammatory prognostic score (IPS) derived from multiple inflammation‐related biomarkers to predict long‐term all‐cause mortality in patients with acute PE.

pmc-13114361.title: The Prognostic Impact of the Ki-67 Proliferation Index in Patients with Surgically Treated Spinal Metastases
pmc-13114361.creator: Saif-Eldin Abedellatif, Marija Janjic, Logman Khalafov, Harun Asoglu, Juliane Dittmer, Muriel Heimann, Mohammed Jaber, Haitham Alenezi, Marieta Ioana Toma, Matthias Schneider, Hartmut Vatter, Motaz Hamed, Mohammed Banat
pmc-13114361.description: Simple SummarySurvival in patients with spinal metastases varies widely, making reliable prognostic tools essential for treatment decisions. Beyond established clinical and imaging-based factors, tumor biology may provide additional insight. This study evaluated whether the proliferation marker Ki-67 can help predict survival in patients undergoing surgery for spinal metastases.

pmc-13152873.title: Effectiveness of GV20-based wearable low-level laser acupoint therapy for pain on head
pmc-13152873.creator: Wen-Fang Lei, Arslan Sadiq, Zhen-Yang Cui, Xu-Bo Wu, Shin-Da Lee
pmc-13152873.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The effectiveness of GV20-based Wearable Low-level Laser Acupoint Therapy for pain on right temporal head was investigated. The study was designed as a triple-blinded, randomized controlled clinical trial. The deep pressure pain targeted by 300g monofilament and Visual Analog Scale (VAS, 0-10) scores on right temporal head were assessed were randomly assigned to wearable LLLAT (650 nm, 5 mW, 30 min, about 9 joule each acupoint) on Baihui (GV20) with four Sishencong (EX-HN1) or sham group (n=24 vs 24).

pmc-13332349.title: Functional Dysphagia Presenting With Severe Subjective Swallowing Difficulty Despite Minimal Objective Findings: A Case Report
pmc-13332349.creator: Fumiyuki Goto, Koichiro Nishiyama, Kenji Okami, Koichiro Wasano
pmc-13332349.description: BackgroundFunctional dysphagia is defined as a persistent or recurrent sensation of abnormal bolus passage without demonstrable structural, inflammatory, or major neuromuscular abnormality. Despite its clinical relevance, otolaryngologic reports of this condition remain limited.Case PresentationWe describe a 71‐year‐old man who presented with progressive swallowing difficulty following a self‐limited pharyngeal infection.

pmc-13389787.title: Toxicological profiling of clinically used chemotherapeutics in zebrafish (Danio rerio) larvae
pmc-13389787.creator: Andrei Nicolae Ceobanu, Alexandru Florin Braniște, Gabriel Mihail Dimofte
pmc-13389787.description: Zebrafish patient-derived xenografts (zPDX) are a powerful emerging platform for personalized oncology, offering a rapid in vivo system for high-throughput chemoprofiling. Recent studies have demonstrated a strong predictive correlation between drug response in zPDX and patient clinical outcomes. However, current protocols show significant variability in drug concentrations, which can hinder comparison across studies.

pmc-13478179.title: PHGDH loss promotes hypoxia tolerance through glycolytic reprogramming and enhanced HIF-1 activity

pmc-13503668.title: Microstructural remodeling and mechanical enhancement of expansive and clayey soils induced by magnetized water
pmc-13503668.creator: Shen-long Wang, Bao-jun Wang, Pei-yang Cheng, Cheng-Cheng Zhang
pmc-13503668.description: The stabilization of expansive and clayey soils remains a persistent challenge in geotechnical engineering. This study investigates the potential of magnetized water—a sustainable, physical treatment method—to enhance the engineering properties of such problematic soils. Through a comparative analysis using expansive and clayey soils from Nanjing, China, we evaluated changes in particle size distribution, Atterberg limits, permeability, compaction, and shear strength.

pmc-13649902.title: Rheuma-VOR – gesundheitsökonomische Bewertung einer frühzeitigen rheumatologischen Diagnostik
pmc-13649902.creator: Juliana Rachel Hoeper, Matthias Dreher, Julian Maximilian Kohl, Marlon Grodd, Johanna Callhoff, Andreas Schwarting, Jan Zeidler
pmc-13649902.description: HintergrundRheuma-VOR wurde initiiert, um lange Wartezeiten bis zur fachärztlichen Diagnosestellung und leitliniengerechte Therapieeinleitung bei rheumatoider Arthritis (RA), Psoriasisarthritis (PsA) und axialen Spondyloarthritiden (axSpA) zu verkürzen.MethodikRheuma-VOR ist eine prospektive, nichtrandomisierte, multizentrische Netzwerkstudie, in die eine gesundheitsökonomische Evaluation eingebettet wurde. Mithilfe eines quasi-experimentellen Kohortendesigns und Propensity-Score-Matching wurde die Interventionsgruppe (Rheuma-VOR) mit der Standardversorgung (Kerndokumentation) verglichen.

pmc-13656465.title: Diagnosing carcinoma origin in ultrasound-guided needle biopsies: a context-driven approach anchored in site-specific immunohistochemical markers
pmc-13656465.creator: Gratiana Hermann, Raluca Ghica, Rares Buiga, Iunia Cebotaru, Daniela Coza, Zeno Sparchez
pmc-13656465.description: BackgroundIn small-biopsy carcinomas, tumor-origin assignment often relies on limited tissue, clinical-radiologic context, morphology, and immunohistochemistry. Although site-specific markers are widely used to support tumor-origin assignment, how often such assignment is supported by site-specific-marker–anchored IHC without CK7/CK20 dependence in context-rich, non-CUP/MUO small-biopsy cohorts has been less explicitly addressed.
